messages.content:
Write a compact standalone deliverable. Lead with the outcome. Every sentence must carry several concrete facts: join related clauses with semicolons and share their subject. Usually use 2–4 short sentences in one paragraph, with no heading, introduction, recap, filler or editing commentary. Target about 35–45 words for verbose source material, expanding only to preserve required meaning.

Preserve ALL unique facts: exact results and scope; exclusions and negations; unknowns; conditions and ordering; evidence IDs; responsible people; next actions. Remove only repetition and conversational framing. Avoid separately restating what a concrete limitation already means. For example, write "The local patch passes 6 tests; Sal must check staging before deployment (patch-proof-2)." instead of six separate sentences about the patch, tests, evidence, locality, next owner and deployment prerequisite. Never convert a plan into completed work or an uncertainty into a fact.

Preserve technical literals byte for byte, including numbers, units, filenames, field names, commands, errors, frontmatter and code blocks. Use clear complete sentences whose referents are identifiable without the source conversation. Do not shorten by hiding any fact behind a generic phrase such as "check first" or "see evidence". Silently verify every source fact before returning only the deliverable.

Copy an already concise source EXACTLY, without additions or rephrasing. Return requested JSON alone with the exact keys and value types. Explicit requests for detail override brevity: retain ordered steps, their reasons, conditions and provenance.

An existing memo rewrite requires an explicit request, preview and approved save through validated memo.write with expected_revision. Stop on conflict. Keep newer text, source transcripts and detailed evidence intact. Draft in one normal model call.

Write the requested deliverable from the supplied source. Preserve every substantive fact, constraint, uncertainty, provenance and next action. Do not invent information. Return only the deliverable, with no account of your editing process.

Deliverable surface: memo.
Write a standalone retention decision.

Source:
The retention decision applies to generated preview artifacts. It does not apply to the original source documents, and that distinction should not be lost in shortening the note. Preview artifacts become eligible for cleanup after seven days without access. Eligibility is not the same as deletion: the first operation produces a preview of the candidates and does not delete them. A pinned artifact is excluded even if it is older than seven days. Applying cleanup requires the exact candidate revision from the preview; if an artifact changes before apply, that artifact is skipped and reported as changed. There is no automatic replay of skipped deletions. The decision is captured in retention-review-2. The next step is to test a pinned artifact and an artifact changed between preview and apply. No assertion has yet been made that those tests have passed, so the note must keep them as next actions.

message.content: Retention decision (retention-review-2): generated preview artifacts are eligible for cleanup after seven days without access; eligibility is not deletion, and the first operation only previews candidates. Pinned artifacts are excluded even if older than seven days. Applying cleanup requires the exact candidate revision from the preview; if an artifact changes before apply, it is skipped and reported as changed, with no automatic replay. This decision does not apply to original source documents. Next actions: test a pinned artifact and an artifact changed between preview and apply; no assertion has been made that these tests have passed.
